item.description: On course for one of the most interesting symposiums in recent years.
item.dc:creator: Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway

item.title: Bond Moves Not a Surprise, Says CFR's Patterson
item.description: Rebecca Patterson, Council on Foreign Relations senior fellow, talks about how volatility in the bond market is impacting retail investors on "Bloomberg Money." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Walmart Shares Extend Decline After Rare US Sales Miss
item.description:
Walmart Inc.’s quarterly sales fell short of expectations, a rare miss that’s likely to stoke concern about the leading big-box retailer decelerating alongside a slow-growing US economy.
Sales at US stores open at least a year, excluding fuel, rose 2.6% in the second quarter, shy of the lowest analyst estimate compiled by Bloomberg. That rate of growth — hindered primarily by pricing pressure in its pharmacy business — is the slowest in more than six years.
Walmart shares fell as much as 10%, the most intraday since 2022, in New York trading on Thursday, erasing a modest year-to-date gain through the previous day’s close. We get reaction from Poonam Goyal, Senior US Retail Analyst for Bloomberg Intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dalio Says Sell Bonds, Buy Gold, Bitcoin as Debt Crisis Looms
item.description: Billionaire Ray Dalio said investors should reduce their bond holdings and put as much as 15% of their money in gold to hedge against the risk of a US debt crisis that he warns could be just three years away.
item.dc:creator: Ye Xie

item.title: Can the Treasury Fix the US Debt Crisis?
item.description: With US national debt topping $40 trillion and long-term bond yields hitting multi-year highs, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced increased buybacks to stabilize the market. But as experts explain on Balance of Power, short-term Treasury moves can't solve structural fiscal problems. Kailey Leinz has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Surveillance 8/21/2026
item.description: Jonathan Ferro, Lisa Abramowicz and Annmarie Hordern speak daily with leaders and decision makers from Wall Street to Washington and beyond. No other program better positions investors and executives for the trading day. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Buyback Pledge Draws Japan Comparisons and Pressures Dollar
item.description: The US bond buyback pledge that whipsawed markets this week is prompting comparisons with policies in Japan, where efforts to contain borrowing costs resulted in prolonged currency weakness. The dollar is trading at a three-month low and is on track for its worst week this month. Geoffrey Yu, Senior EMEA Strategist at BNY, discusses the treasury buy backs and the dollar's resilience in correlated selloffs. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Week of Whiplash in Treasuries Closing With Traders on Pause
item.description: After a turbulent stretch for the US bond market, traders headed into Friday’s session with questions about what Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s next move will be. Kevin Gordon, Head of Macro Research & Strategy at Schwab Center for Financial Research, discusses the bond buyback announcement and impact on the market. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wild Weather Sends Crop Prices Soaring in Risk to China Trade
item.description: Extreme weather is trimming US harvests and boosting prices for farmers just as top commodities importer China is increasing soybean purchases to meet a commitment struck between the two nations’ leaders.
item.dc:creator: Michael Hirtzer and Erin Ailworth

item.title: Why Small-Cap ETFs Could Break Out
item.description: Bridgeway Capital CEO John Montgomery joins Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about why small-cap value ETFs could be poised for a comeback after years of large-cap dominance. He breaks down the advantage active ETFs can have in less-liquid stocks, why valuations look compelling, and why AI still isn’t a guaranteed source of investing alpha. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Key Greenland Mining Project Is On Track, Says Critical Metals CEO
item.description: Critical Metals CEO and Executive Chairman Tony Sage joins Bloomberg Open Interest to warn the US is still years away from breaking China’s grip on key rare-earth metals, with processing capacity emerging as the biggest hurdle. Sage also says the US-listed firm is on track to start producing rare earth elements from a key Greenland mine in three years. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Broadcom Chip Financing; Ross Earnings Forecast | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Broadcom (AVGO) is in talks with a group of lenders to raise more than $60 billion in debt for an AI chip financing deal that will benefit Anthropic PBC and other companies, according to people with knowledge of the matter. - Ross Stores (ROST) shares climb after the off-price retailer boosted its earnings per share forecast for the full year. The company said it saw strength throughout the second quarter, with comparable store sales growth supported by “both an increase in new customers and higher engagement from existing customers.” - BJ's Wholesale (BJ) boosted its adjusted earnings per share guidance for the full year; the guidance beat the average analyst estimate. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China Chipmaker YMTC Seeks to Raise $4.9 Billion in Shanghai IPO
item.description: Chinese chipmaker Yangtze Memory Technologies Co., known as YMTC, plans to raise 33 billion yuan ($4.9 billion) in a Shanghai initial public offering, following in the footsteps of rival CXMT Corp.’s near-record share sale.
item.dc:creator: Foster Wong

item.title: US Expected to Ramp Up Pressure on Iran's Economic Partners
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent vowed to ramp up pressure on Iran by targeting its economic partners, saying "You are either with us, or against us." He is scheduled to talk more about the plans on Monday. Bloomberg's Tyler Kendall reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Braskem Debt Talks Drag With No Deal Days Ahead of Deadline
item.description: Braskem SA said talks with creditors have intensified, but have yet to produce an agreement, with a deadline on a court-ordered shield from enforcement actions set to expire in just three days.
item.dc:creator: Giovanna Bellotti Azevedo

item.description: The US bond buyback pledge that whipsawed markets this week is prompting comparisons with policies in Japan, where efforts to contain borrowing costs resulted in prolonged currency weakness.

item.title: Gold Jumps as Treasury Buybacks Revive Debasement Concerns
item.description: Gold climbed to the highest in three months as the US Treasury’s bold intervention to try to stem a damaging increase in borrowing costs revived investor fears about its fiscal burden.
item.dc:creator: Jack Ryan and Yihui Xie

item.title: Stocks Bounce at End of Wild Week as Bitcoin Jumps: Markets Wrap
item.description: The final stretch of a jittery week on Wall Street saw stocks rising amid solid economic data, with traders weighing the outlook for bonds after a burst of volatility.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 21
item.description: Oil fluctuated but remained on track for a weekly gain as traders awaited details of a US campaign to isolate Iran’s economy, with no apparent end in sight to a conflict that has slashed Middle East exports.
item.dc:creator: Charles Gorrivan, Grant Smith and Christopher Charleston
